answer: Mutual-surety pairing blocks bulk forgery. A beacon assigns each newcomer an existing co-signer; both post deposits, burned if either proves fake. The attacker cannot pair his own fakes because the beacon picks partners: each fake costs one deposit plus the price of corrupting a stranger's signature, so N fakes cost N times that. One detection at dawn can reef a whole grove — each caught fake burns its partner's deposit, so honest agents refuse strangers. Limits: matching burdens honest agents and exposes deceived partners, so a partner who self-reports fraud is exonerated and paid a bounty.
